subtitle: How a Hill King Bound His People’s Memory into Verse and Water

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a lone king standing between a vast stepped tank and ghostly scrolls swirling in the sky
panels.action: Dharma Manikya I stands at the edge of a great tank, Dharmasagar, his reflection rippling in the water as translucent scrolls of Bengali verse coil above him like clouds over the forests of Tripura.

dialogue.text: In the fifteenth century, as rivers shifted and kingdoms fought, Dharma Manikya of Tripura did something strange for a warrior king: he stopped to write down his people’s past.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी में, नदियाँ बदल रहीं, राज्य लड़ रहे थे, तभी त्रिपुरा के धर्म माणिक्य ने योद्धा होते हुए भी अनोखा काम किया – अपनी जाति का अतीत लिखने बैठ गए।

panels.shot: wide aerial shot over dense green hills fading into the plains of Bengal, with faint outlines of rival kingdoms at the horizons
panels.action: From above, the forested hills of Tripura roll down into misty plains where distant fort-towns of Bengal and Arakan glimmer, Dharma Manikya I riding a small escort along a ridge path.

dialogue.text: Around 1430, the Manikya kingdom stood at a crossroads of hills and plains, between Bengal’s sultans, Arakan’s coast, and older Kokborok-speaking chiefdoms rooted in these forests.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1430 में माणिक्य राज्य पहाड़ और मैदानी चौराहे पर था – बंगाल के सुल्तान, अराकान का तट, और इन जंगलों में जमे पुराने ककबोरोक बोलने वाले सरदारों के बीच।

panels.shot: medium shot at a riverbank ferry, with the king dismounting and touching the water
panels.action: Dharma Manikya I, in travel robes, steps down from his horse at the bank of a broad river, bowing to touch the water while attendants hold the reins behind him.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala itself remembers him returning from pilgrimage, moving along rivers and roads toward Benares, pausing at shrines and ferries that tied Tripura to the wider world.

i18n.hi: राजमाला बताती है, वह तीर्थ से लौटते हुए नदियों–सड़कों से होते बनारस की ओर चले, राह में उन देवस्थानों और घाटों पर रुके जो त्रिपुरा को बड़े संसार से जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Benares ghats at dawn, with the king among pilgrims
panels.action: At dawn on the ghats of Benares, smoke from lamps curls into the grey sky as Dharma Manikya I stands barefoot among pilgrims, gazing at priests reciting aloud from palm-leaf manuscripts.

dialogue.text: In Benares, he would have seen another kind of power: Brahmins with palm-leaf books, lineages recited by heart, histories woven into ritual, binding kings to stories older than their crowns.

i18n.hi: बनारस में उन्होंने एक और ताकत देखी होगी – ताड़पत्रों वाले ब्राह्मण, ज़ुबानी वंशावलियाँ, इतिहास जो पूजा में बुना था, राजाओं को ताजों से भी पुराने किस्सों से बाँधता हुआ।

panels.shot: close-up on the king’s thoughtful face, light from an oil lamp flickering
panels.action: An oil lamp’s flame lights one side of Dharma Manikya I’s face as he watches an elderly scholar chant, the reflection of moving script visible in his eyes.

dialogue.speaker: dharma_manikya_i
dialogue.text: Our hills remember in song. Who will hear us if the songs are lost?

i18n.hi: हमारे पहाड़ गीतों में याद रखते हैं। गीत खोए तो हमें कौन सुनेगा?

panels.shot: transition wide shot of the king’s return caravan entering a hill capital
panels.action: Dust rises as Dharma Manikya I’s caravan winds back into his hill capital, banners bearing the Manikya emblem fluttering over timber halls and bamboo palisades.

dialogue.text: When he returned to Tripura, he carried more than gifts and merits. He carried a question: how should a hill kingdom, with its own tongue and gods, speak to this new world of chronicles?

i18n.hi: जब वह त्रिपुरा लौटे, हाथ में केवल भेंट और पुण्य नहीं थे। एक सवाल भी था – अपनी बोली और देवताओं वाला पहाड़ी राज्य इस नए इतिहास–जगत से कैसे बात करे?

panels.shot: interior medium shot in a wooden hall, king seated with two learned poets before him
panels.action: Inside a wooden audience hall, Dharma Manikya I sits on a low throne as two Bengali-versed poets, Sukreswar and Vaneswar, sit cross-legged before him with writing boards and ink pots.

dialogue.text: The Rajmala names the men he chose: Sukreswar and Vaneswar. Under his order they would shape Tripura’s memories into Bengali verse, drawing from older Kokborok tales and a lost Rajratnakar.

i18n.hi: राजमाला दो नाम दर्ज करती है – शुकेश्वर और वनेश्वर। उसके हुक्म से वे त्रिपुरा की स्मृतियों को बंगला पद्य में ढालते हैं, पुराने ककबोरोक किस्सों और खोए राजरत्नाकर से रेखाएँ खींचते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot focused on the king speaking firmly to the poets, with attendants listening
panels.action: Dharma Manikya I leans forward, one hand raised in measured command, as the two poets bow their heads and attendants stand silently behind them.

dialogue.speaker: dharma_manikya_i
dialogue.text: Write our line as we remember it, yet in a tongue the plains will read.

i18n.hi: हमारी वंश–कथा वैसे ही लिखो, जैसा हम कहते हैं, पर ऐसी ज़ुबान में जो मैदानी पढ़ सकें।

panels.shot: montage-style medium shot of scribes at work, with faint overlay of hill bards performing
panels.action: Scribes bend over palm leaves, stylus scratching, while in a ghosted overlay behind them hill bards in traditional dress sing with drums before a village fire.

dialogue.text: Behind their neat lines lay older voices in Kokborok and Koloma script, an oral and written memory already centuries deep, now being recast into Sanskritic frames and Bengali metres.

i18n.hi: उनकी सजी पंक्तियों के पीछे ककबोरोक और कोलोमा लिपि की पुरानी आवाज़ें थीं – सदियों पुरानी मौखिक–लिखित यादें, जिन्हें अब संस्कृतनुमा ढाँचे और बंगाली छंदों में ढाला जा रहा था।

panels.shot: close-up of a palm-leaf manuscript being unrolled before the king
panels.action: A courtier unrolls a fresh palm-leaf manuscript, delicate characters incised and blackened, as Dharma Manikya I’s hand rests on the edge, steady but tense.

dialogue.text: The first canto of the Rajmala took shape at his court, tracing Manikya origins and conquests. Its kings are real, its pride clear, but its early genealogy is tangled and often at odds with other evidence.

i18n.hi: राजमाला का पहला सर्ग उसके दरबार में बना – माणिक्य कुल की उत्पत्ति और विजय रेखता हुआ। राजा असली हैं, गर्व साफ है, पर शुरुआती वंशावली उलझी है और कई जगह दूसरे सबूतों से टकराती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king in discussion with priests and elders around the manuscript
panels.action: Seated around the opened manuscript, Dharma Manikya I listens as a priest, a hill elder, and a Brahmin scholar gesture and debate, pointing to different lines.

dialogue.text: Even at the moment of writing, memory was being argued: lineage stretched, ancestors reordered, hill deities aligned with Puranic gods. The Rajmala preserved, but it also reshaped, what came before.

i18n.hi: उसी समय याद पर बहस चल रही थी – वंश खींचे जा रहे थे, पूर्वजों की कतार बदली जा रही थी, पहाड़ी देवताओं को पुराणिक देवों से जोड़ा जा रहा था। राजमाला ने बचाया भी, और बदल भी दिया, जो पहले था।

panels.shot: wide conceptual shot showing a timeline fading into mist with later hands revising earlier scrolls
panels.action: A spectral sequence of scrolls stretches into the mist, with shadowy later scribes scratching corrections onto older leaves, some passages darkened, others scraped away.

dialogue.text: Later cantos would alter the early tale, adding episodes, smoothing defeats, fitting Tripura into changing politics. For modern historians, the Rajmala is a vital witness—and an interested one.

i18n.hi: बाद के सर्गों ने शुरुआती कथा को और मोड़ा – नए प्रसंग जोड़े, हारें मुलायम कीं, बदलती सियासत में त्रिपुरा को नए सांचे में फिट किया। आज के इतिहासकारों के लिए राजमाला गवाह भी है, और पक्षधर भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of the king inspecting the site of the future Dharmasagar tank with engineers
panels.action: On a flat plain near Comilla, Dharma Manikya I stands with builders and surveyors, gesturing toward a marked-out rectangle where villagers and workers gather, the outline of a vast tank traced in the earth.

dialogue.text: Tradition in Comilla links the same king to another monument of memory: Dharmasagar, a great tank said to have been completed around 1458, spreading Tripura’s reach into the plains with water and stone.

i18n.hi: कुमिल्ला की परंपरा उसी राजा को एक और स्मृति–चिह्न से जोड़ती है – धर्मसागर, एक विशाल तालाब, जो लगभग 1458 में पूरा हुआ माना जाता है, पानी और पत्थर से त्रिपुरा को मैदानों तक फैलाते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king kneeling to pick up a handful of soil at the tank site
panels.action: Dharma Manikya I kneels, scooping a handful of dry soil that crumbles between his fingers as workers in the background begin digging with baskets and spades.

dialogue.speaker: dharma_manikya_i
dialogue.text: Let this water remember us when words fade.

i18n.hi: जब शब्द मिट जाएँ, ये पानी हमें याद रखें।

panels.shot: wide shot of the completed Dharmasagar tank filled with water, lined by steps and trees
panels.action: The Dharmasagar tank lies full and still, broad stone steps descending to its surface, trees and small shrines dotting the banks, villagers gathering with pots and cattle at the edges.

dialogue.text: Dharmasagar anchored settlement and ritual, a reservoir that outlived palaces. Archaeology and local memory point back to Dharma Manikya, tying his name to both text and water.

i18n.hi: धर्मसागर ने बसावट और पूजा को थामे रखा – ऐसा सरोवर जो महलों से ज्यादा जीया। खुदाई और लोक–स्मृति दोनों उंगली धर्म माणिक्य पर टिकाती हैं – उनका नाम ग्रंथ और पानी दोनों से जुड़ता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king at court receiving a coastal envoy with a map showing Arakan
panels.action: In his court, Dharma Manikya I listens as a coastal envoy unfurls a rough map showing Tripura’s hills, the plains, and the Arakan coast, ships sketched along the shore.

dialogue.text: Other traditions, from Arakan, remember him too—as a helper of Min Saw Mon in the struggles of that coastal kingdom. The details are debated, but they show Tripura in a wider Burmese–Bengal theatre.

i18n.hi: एक और धारा, अराकान की, उन्हें याद करती है – तटीय राज्य के संघर्षों में मिन सॉ मॉन के मददगार के रूप में। विवरण पर झगड़ा है, पर इससे त्रिपुरा का चेहरा बड़े बर्मा–बंगाल रंगमंच पर दिखता है।

panels.shot: conceptual wide shot juxtaposing battle standards with a manuscript and a tank
panels.action: On a hazy horizon, battle standards and helmets recede, while in the foreground a palm-leaf manuscript lies beside the placid Dharmasagar tank under a spreading tree.

dialogue.text: Dharma Manikya’s campaigns against Bengal’s frontiers have left fewer traces than his chronicle and his tank. Steel rusts quickly; verse and water, when tended, endure in quieter ways.

i18n.hi: धर्म माणिक्य की बंगाल सीमा पर चढ़ाइयाँ, उनकी किताब और उनके तालाब जितना निशान नहीं छोड़ पाईं। लोहा जल्दी जंग खाता है; संभाली हुई कविता और पानी चुपचाप ज्यादा देर टिकते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of a modern researcher’s hands handling an old Rajmala manuscript in a library
panels.action: Modern hands in a quiet library gently lift a brittle Rajmala manuscript, its edges frayed, as a magnifying glass reveals the fine Bengali script carved centuries ago.

dialogue.text: Today, scholars read the Rajmala against inscriptions, Kokborok manuscripts, and oral lore, peeling back layers of courtly revision to glimpse the older Tripura that sang beneath the verses.

i18n.hi: आज विद्वान राजमाला को शिलालेखों, ककबोरोक पांडुलिपियों और लोक–कथाओं के साथ रखकर पढ़ते हैं, दरबारी घिस–पिट के पीछे की परतें खुरचते हैं, ताकि पद्यों के नीचे गाती पुरानी त्रिपुरा झलक सके।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the king’s silhouette reflected alongside stars in the Dharmasagar water at night
panels.action: At night, the surface of Dharmasagar mirrors stars and the faint silhouette of Dharma Manikya I, standing unseen at the edge, his figure rippling with the slightest breeze across the water.

dialogue.text: By ordering the Rajmala and digging Dharmasagar, Dharma Manikya turned a hill people’s memory into text and stone—so that later generations could argue with legend instead of living only inside it.

i18n.hi: राजमाला का हुक्म देकर और धर्मसागर खुदवाकर, धर्म माणिक्य ने पहाड़ों की याद को शब्द और पत्थर में बांध दिया – ताकि अगली पीढ़ियाँ दंतकथाओं से बहस कर सकें, न कि केवल उनमें कैद होकर जीएँ।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Hill King Bound His People’s Memory into Verse and Water
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक पहाड़ी राजा ने यादें बांध दीं काव्य और पानी में
